'''Tarbut V'Torah Community Day School (TVT)''' is a private [[Judaism|Jewish]] non-denominational Community Day School located in southern [[Irvine, California]], in northern [[Orange County, California|Orange County]].<ref name="auto">Martin Aaron Brower (2010). [https://books.google.com/books?id=0Gh0fIdgDTIC&dq=%22Tarbut+V%27Torah%22&pg=PA135 ''Orange County Jew: a Memoir'']</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.archdaily.com/912759/tarbut-vtorah-community-day-school-lpa|title=Tarbut V'Torah Community Day School / LPA|date=March 8, 2019|website=ArchDaily}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperialbeachnewsca.com/news/article_5f0dec56-1559-11ea-9f24-077f9fcd3e2d.html|title=South Bay Union School District Families Celebrate Thanksgiving|first=Pete|last=Salisbury|website=Eagle & Time|date=November 29, 2019}}</ref>  The school is divided into separate sections: the Lower School serves grades TK-5, and the Upper School serves grades 6-12.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto5">Jane Yu (July 15, 2013). [https://www.ocbj.com/news/2013/jul/15/jewish-school-irvine-names-new-ceo/ "Jewish School in Irvine Names New CEO,"] ''Orange County Business Journal''.</ref>  The schools are located on its {{convert|21.5|acre|m2|adj=on}} campus that was donated by the [[Henry Samueli|Samueli family]] and other donors.<ref name="auto5"/><ref name="auto7">{{Cite web|url=http://www.asceoc.org/awards/nominee-details/2018_-_tarbut_v_torah_phase_iii_phase_iv/2018|title=Awards and Nominations - 2018 - Tarbut V' Torah Phase III & Phase IV |website= American Society of Civil Engineers - Orange County Branch}}</ref> The school has been recognized as a [[Blue Ribbon Schools Program|Blue Ribbon School]].

== History ==

Founded in 1991 by [[Holocaust survivor]] Irving "Papa" Gelman, Tarbut V'Torah Community Day School (TVT), is an elementary, middle, and high school educational facility located in [[Irvine, California]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto5"/><ref name="OCB"/> Gelman died in 2018.<ref name="OCB">{{Cite news|url=https://www.ocbj.com/news/2018/mar/05/irving-papa-gelman-dies/|title=Irving "Papa" Gelman Dies|last=Weitzner|first=Pete|date=March 5, 2018|work=Orange County Business Journal|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref>

The school sits on a {{convert|10.5|acre|m2|adj=on}} campus, opened in 1997 with more than 800 students.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto5"/><ref name="OCB"/>  The school became the second Jewish school in [[Orange County, California|Orange County]] to be cited among the 465 National Distinguished [[Blue Ribbon Schools Program|Blue Ribbon Schools]] in California when the designation was conferred during the 1998-1999 school year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.ed.gov/programs/nclbbrs/list-1982.pdf|title=BLUE RIBBON SCHOOLS PROGRAM; Schools Recognized 1982-1983 Through 1999-2002|publisher=Blue Ribbon Schools Program Knowledge Applications Division, U.S. Department of Education}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lAQEAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Tarbut+V%27Torah%22&pg=PA46|title=Teaching Character |work=Orange Coast Magazine|date=May 5, 2003|author=Darcy Rice|publisher=Emmis Communications|via=Google Books}}</ref>  The school graduated its first senior class in 2001.<ref name="auto1"/>

The campus expanded the upper school in September 2002:  An area of {{convert|11|acre|m2}} was added and a new middle and high school was constructed to accommodate increased enrollment for all grade levels.  The campus encompasses {{convert|21.5|acre|m2}} and {{convert|150000|sqft|m2|-3}} of structures.<ref name="auto7"/>  In 2005-06, a record 645 students (grades K-12) enrolled at TVT, making it the eighth-largest Jewish Community Day School in the United States. In 2013, Tarbut V’Torah named teacher Jeffrey Davis its new chief executive.<ref name="auto5"/>  That year it had 603 students and 84 faculty members, a $13 million operating budget, and total assets of about $42 million.<ref name="auto5"/>

The name "Tarbut" is inspired by the [[Tarbut]] schools created by the [[Yiddish]]-speaking community of pre-World War II [[Eastern Europe]].  The founder of Tarbut V'Torah, Irving Gelman, attended one of these schools. Tarbut V'Torah, translated from [[Hebrew]], simply means culture & [[Torah]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=__0DAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Tarbut+V%27Torah%22&pg=PA6|author=Barbara DeMarco Barrett|title=Biblical Passages|work=Orange Coast Magazine|date=April 5, 1998|publisher=Emmis Communications|via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Dv4DAAAAMBAJ&q=%22Tarbut+V%27Torah%22&pg=PA26|author=Susannah Abbey|title=Exile no more|work=Orange Coast Magazine|date=September 5, 1998|publisher=Emmis Communications|via=Google Books}}</ref> Tarbut schools had a curriculum that was secular and included science, humanities, and Hebrew studies, including Jewish history.  Today, other Tarbut schools exist in [[Colegio Tarbut|Argentina]] and in [http://www.tarbut.edu.mx/ Mexico], but there is no formal affiliation between either of those schools and Tarbut v'Torah.

== Athletics ==

TVT's athletics department is divided into Middle School athletics and High School athletics.

Tarbut V' Torah's middle school athletic program competes in the Tri-Way League, consisting of 10 other private schools throughout Orange County. The boys field three teams which include [[flag football]], [[basketball]], and [[soccer]], while the girls compete in [[volleyball]], basketball, and soccer.

TVT's high school athletic program has more than 10 teams. In the fall, girls compete in volleyball (ranked in Division 5) and [[tennis]], and both boys and girls compete in [[cross country running]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/story/2020-01-08/brethren-christians-shawnee-starke-named-to-all-express-league-second-team-in-girls-volleyball|title=Brethren Christian's Shawnee Starke named to All-Express League second team in girls' volleyball|date=January 9, 2020|website=Daily Pilot}}</ref>  In the winter, both boys and girls compete in soccer; in addition, TVT has a winter basketball team, which is ranked in Division 5/the Express League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/story/2020-01-23/sage-hill-boys-soccer-falls-to-tarbut-vtorah|title=Sage Hill boys' soccer falls to Tarbut V'Torah|date=January 24, 2020|website=Daily Pilot|author=Andrew Turner}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/story/2020-02-12/estancia-boys-basketball-beats-tarbut-vtorah-for-first-cif-playoff-win-since-2014|title=Estancia boys' basketball routs Tarbut V'Torah for first CIF playoff win since 2014|date=February 13, 2020|website=Daily Pilot}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/tn-dpt-sp-nb-pacifica-christian-tarbut-v-torah-20180124-story.html|title=Pacifica Christian Orange County girls' soccer stays hot, edges Tarbut V'Torah|date=January 25, 2018|website=Daily Pilot}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/orange-county-boys-soccer-all-league-teams-2019-20|title=Orange County boys soccer: All-league teams 2019-20|date=March 27, 2020|work=The Orange County Register}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/orange-county-boys-basketball-all-league-teams-2019-20|title=Orange County boys basketball: All-league teams 2019-20|date=March 25, 2020|work=The Orange County Register}}</ref> In the spring, boys can play tennis, [[baseball]], [[swimming (sport)|swimming]], and volleyball, and the girls can play in swimming and [[softball]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://syvnews.com/sports/high-school/popkin-calls-it-a-career/article_35aa78b8-ba18-5032-8891-f4c48dd594f5.html|title=Popkin calls it a career|first=Kenny |last=Cress|website=Santa Ynez Valley News|date=May 11, 2016}}</ref>

===Girls' soccer===
[[Camille Levin]] attended Tarbut V' Torah, where she played soccer on a co-ed team for at least one season and was named to the [[NSCAA]] All-America team in 2006 and 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Cammy-Levin-Stanford-soccer-s-do-it-all-player-2455036.php|title=Cammy Levin, Stanford soccer's do-it-all player|first=Tom|last=FitzGerald|date=December 2, 2010|website=SFGate}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Necessity forces girls to take field with … ick!|url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/girls-60290-boys-team.html|work=Orange County Register|access-date=September 17, 2013|date=March 9, 2007|author=Marcia C. Smith}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Corona's Munerlyn lifts U.S. to title|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/soccer/post/_/id/16406/coronas-munerlyn-lifts-u-s-to-title|publisher=ESPN|access-date=September 12, 2013|date=May 12, 2012|author=Scott French}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jwa.org/thisweek/dec/04/2011/camille-levin|title=Stanford wins NCAA College Cup with help from Jewish soccer star, Camille Levin|date=December 4, 2011|website=Jewish Women's Archive}}</ref> She went on to play for the [[Stanford Cardinal women's soccer|Stanford Cardinal women's soccer team]]  that won the [[2011 NCAA Division I Women's Soccer Tournament]], and a career in which she in 2013 was the captain of the [[United States women's national under-23 soccer team|United States U-23 women's national soccer team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=USA U23 Captain signs for Wanderers|url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/wswanderersfc/news-display/USA-U23-Captain-signs-for-Wanderers/79377|publisher=Football Australia|access-date=November 30, 2013|date=November 30, 2013}}</ref>

Camille Levin's younger sister [[Savannah Levin]] (class of 2013) also played soccer for the school for four years, and was named league MVP in soccer all four years, as well as a four-time first team all-league selection.<ref name="autox">{{Cite web|url=https://usctrojans.com/sports/womens-soccer/roster/savannah-levin/2636|title=Savannah Levin - Women's Soccer|website=USC Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/savannah-levin/vOTJMvTrEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm|title=Savannah Levin's High School Timeline|website=MaxPreps.com}}</ref> She went on to play for the [[USC Trojans women's soccer|USC Trojans women's soccer team]] that won the [[2016 NCAA Division I Women's Soccer Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://usctrojans.com/news/2016/12/4/National_Champs_No_7_Trojans_Defeat_No_1_West_Virginia_3_1_to_Earn_Program_s_Second_Title.aspx|title=NATIONAL CHAMPS NO. 7 TROJANS DEFEAT NO. 1 WEST VIRGINIA 3-1 TO EARN PROGRAM'S SECOND TITLE|access-date=July 9, 2018|date=December 4, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailynews.com/sports/20161204/usc-women-win-ncaa-soccer-championship|title=USC women's soccer beats West Virginia to win College Cup|website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=December 4, 2016}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2014 and as a junior in 2015 she earned [[Pac-12]] All-Academic honorable mention.<ref name="autox"/>

Carly Malatskey, a 2016 graduate of Tarbut V’ Torah High School who attended it from kindergarten on, captained the girls' soccer team from 2013–16, and scored 73 goals in 2015-16, an Orange County record and second all-time in [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/tn-dpt-sp-0709-carly-malatskey-stanford-soccer-20160717-story.html|title=Soccer: Malatskey dancing by defenders|date=July 17, 2016|website=Daily Pilot|author=Matt Szabo}}</ref><ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://gostanford.com/sports/womens-soccer/roster/carly-malatskey/16287|title=Carly Malatskey - Women's Soccer|website=Stanford University Athletics}}</ref><ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/tarbut-vtorah-irvine-calif-soccer-star-carly-malatskey-knows-how-to-put-the-ball-in-the-net|title=Tarbut V'Torah (Irvine, Calif.) soccer star Carly Malatskey knows how to put the ball in the net|date=March 31, 2016|work=USA Today}}</ref> With her playing the team was three-time [[San Joaquin League]] Champion (2014–16), as she was three-time San Joaquin League Player of the Year (2014–16) and led Orange County in goals each of the three years.<ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto3"/> She now plays for the Stanford Cardinal women's soccer team, with whom she has twice won the NCAA Division I Women's Soccer Tournament.<ref name="auto4"/>
